**Klynge MIDT** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in the Danish healthcare system [^src5]. It is one of the local organizational units monitored by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to evaluate and improve the clinical quality of treatment for [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1]. 

The cluster is significant for its performance across various national quality indicators. Notably, Klynge MIDT successfully met the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 93.9% [^src1]. It also met the standards for 1-year and 2-year treatment coverage (Indicators 4a1 and 4a2), scoring 92.3% and 92.5% respectively [^src2]. However, the cluster did not meet the standard for Indicator 4b, which tracks the frequency of annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOAC treatment, recording a result of 89.4% [^src3].

Beyond treatment coverage, Klynge MIDT is evaluated on patient outcomes and complications. The cluster's data contributes to national geographic distributions of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) incidence among atrial fibrillation patients, which ranges across health clusters from [0%-0.8%] to ]2.8%-100%] [^src4]. Furthermore, the cluster is monitored for severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 11) and the development of heart failure within one year (Indicator 15) [^src6], as well as mortality rates and other supplementary clinical outcomes [^src7]. 

Alongside other regional clusters such as [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]] and [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]], Klynge MIDT's performance data is essential for benchmarking, identifying local variations in clinical practice, and guiding hierarchical quality improvement strategies across the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
